title: Add Service at another location copies the work at this location's rates
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in to the Maintenance Reminders QA build as an Owner/Admin (any user who can open Settings > Maintenance and create and edit work orders and customers). The organization has two locations, for example 'Calgary South' (where the schedule is built) and 'Lethbridge'.
  2. At Calgary South, in Settings > Maintenance, give PM-A of 'ZZAUTOTEST Highway Tractor PM' these canned lines: 'Engine oil and filter change' with labour type Mechanical, 1.2 hours, tech time 1.0 and two parts; 'Chassis lubrication' fixed price; 'Air filter inspection' with a labour type that does not exist at Lethbridge, 0.3 hours; 'Brake adjustment check' with no labour type.
  3. At Lethbridge note the labour rates: Mechanical (for example $160.00 an hour) and the default labour type (for example $145.00 an hour).
  4. Enroll unit 'ZZAUTOTEST 402' on that schedule so PM-A reads Overdue.
  5. In the header choose Lethbridge, then create a work order for the unit (New Work Order).
custom_steps:
1. Expand the Maintenance schedule card and read the PM-A row and its (i).
  2. Press Add Service, read the window's preview, and press Add.
  3. Open the Lines tab and read each new line: name, description, hours, tech time, labour type, rate, price, parts and its line note.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The row reads exactly as at Calgary South (for example PM-A, Overdue · Aug 2026, 4 lines · 2.8 hours, Add Service) with an (i): PM-A's lines were set up at Calgary South. We add the same work here at Lethbridge's rates. Parts are not added; each line's note lists the parts Calgary South uses, for reference.
  • The Add Service preview lists no parts.
  • Four new lines carry the same names, descriptions, hours and tech time; no parts are added and no Calgary South price is copied.
  • 'Engine oil and filter change' takes Lethbridge's Mechanical rate: 1.2 × $160.00 = $192.00.
  • 'Air filter inspection' takes Lethbridge's default labour type: 0.3 × $145.00 = $43.50.
  • 'Chassis lubrication', fixed price at Calgary South, is priced the same way here.
  • 'Brake adjustment check', with no labour type at Calgary South, is copied with none and is not priced.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-3780 (Maintenance Reminders); story SV-10572 (S16, The maintenance panel on a work order); Chunk 2 MR (Confluence 897679389) as edited 5 October 2026, S16; read 6 Oct 2026. Source-verified 6 October 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S16-R21: “At a location other than the home location, the row reads exactly as it does at home, for example PM-A, Overdue · Aug 2026, 4 lines · 2.8 hours, Add Service, with an (i) beside it: PM-A's lines were set up at Calgary South. We add the same work here at Lethbridge's rates. Parts are not added; each line's note lists the parts Calgary South uses, for reference”
  • S16-R24: “The Add Service modal is the standard one at every location. At a location other than the home location its preview lists no parts, because none are added; the card's (i) of S16-R21 is the only place that explains the copy”
  • S16-N6: “Add Service at a location other than the schedule's home location adds the same work, not the home location's lines: each canned line's name, description and hours, as new lines at this location's rates. Prices and parts are not copied, because both are kept per location. Tracking and completion stay organization-wide, per S18-R12”
  • S16-R22: “Each copied line takes this location's labour type of the same name, or this location's default labour type where none matches, and is priced at that labour type's rate. A line that is fixed price at the home location is priced the same way here. A copied line carries the home line's tech time as well as its hours. A home line with no labour type is copied with none, so it is not priced, as at home”
